frequency_question: How often do such announced tariffs actually go into effect within the stated short window rather than being averted by a deal or delay?
membership_rule: Includes formal executive announcements of broad import tariffs on specific major allies/neighbors with a designated effective date within 60 days. Excludes standard statutory Section 301 or AD/CVD administrative tariff escalations that follow multi-month bureaucratic investigations.

cases.name: 2018 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs on Canada/Mexico (June implementation)
2019 Proposed Tariffs on all Mexican Goods (threatened June 2019)
2025/2026 BRICS Secondary Tariff Threats (short deadline announcements)

coverage_note: 4 named; believed to represent the primary modern instances of immediate executive tariff threats used as negotiation leverage.
known_gaps: Sample size is small because sweeping executive tariff threats with sub-2-month hard deadlines are rare outside of specific administration negotiating playbooks.
skeleton: 4 named historical comparable showdowns involving high-level tariff threats with short fuses against major trading partners.
multiplier: 1/4 base implementation rate from historical reference class of immediate leverage threats.
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as it relies on executive branch tariff deployment patterns.
